import SafeLearning.CompleteFoundationsNormExercises
import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Module.Convex

set_option autoImplicit false
set_option relaxedAutoImplicit false
set_option maxHeartbeats 1200000
noncomputable section
open Set
open scoped BigOperators ENNReal

namespace SafeLearning.CompleteFoundationsLiteralNorm28
open CompleteFoundationsNormDuality

section Finite
variable {I : Type*} [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]

def sourcePNorm (p : ℝ≥0∞) (x : I → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ‖(WithLp.toLp p x : PiLp p (fun _ : I => ℝ))‖

theorem actual_every_source_p_norm_has_all_three_norm_axioms (p : ℝ≥0∞)
    [Fact (1 ≤ p)] (x y : I → ℝ) (a : ℝ) :
    (sourcePNorm p x=0 ↔ x=0) ∧
    sourcePNorm p (a • x)=|a| * sourcePNorm p x ∧
    sourcePNorm p (x+y) ≤ sourcePNorm p x+sourcePNorm p y := by
  refine ⟨by simp [sourcePNorm],?_,?_⟩
  · simp [sourcePNorm,norm_smul,Real.norm_eq_abs]
  · simpa [sourcePNorm] using
      norm_add_le (WithLp.toLp p x : PiLp p (fun _ : I => ℝ)) (WithLp.toLp p y)

theorem actual_all_finite_source_p_norms_have_the_printed_rpow_formula (p : ℝ≥0∞)
    [Fact (1 ≤ p)] (hp : p≠∞) (x : I → ℝ) :
    sourcePNorm p x=(∑ i,|x i|^p.toReal)^(1/p.toReal) := by
  simpa only [sourcePNorm,Real.norm_eq_abs,PiLp.toLp_apply] using
    PiLp.norm_eq_sum (p.toReal_pos_iff_ne_top.mpr hp)
      (WithLp.toLp p x : PiLp p (fun _ : I => ℝ))

theorem actual_infinity_source_norm_is_the_coordinate_supremum (x : I → ℝ) :
    sourcePNorm ∞ x=‖x‖ ∧ sourcePNorm ∞ x=⨆ i,|x i| := by
  refine ⟨PiLp.norm_toLp x,?_⟩
  simpa only [sourcePNorm,Real.norm_eq_abs,PiLp.toLp_apply] using
    PiLp.norm_eq_ciSup (WithLp.toLp ∞ x : PiLp ∞ (fun _ : I => ℝ))

theorem actual_infinity_source_norm_attains_the_coordinate_maximum [Nonempty I]
    (x : I → ℝ) : ∃ i : I, sourcePNorm ∞ x=|x i| ∧ ∀ j,|x j| ≤ |x i| := by
  obtain ⟨i,hi,hm⟩ := Finset.exists_max_image Finset.univ (fun j : I => |x j|)
    Finset.univ_nonempty
  have hmax : ∀ j,|x j| ≤ |x i| := fun j => hm j (Finset.mem_univ j)
  refine ⟨i,?_,hmax⟩
  rw [(actual_infinity_source_norm_is_the_coordinate_supremum x).1]
  apply le_antisymm
  · exact (pi_norm_le_iff_of_nonneg (abs_nonneg (x i))).mpr
      (fun j => by simpa only [Real.norm_eq_abs] using hmax j)
  · simpa only [Real.norm_eq_abs] using norm_le_pi_norm x i

theorem actual_one_source_norm_is_sum_absolute_values (x : I → ℝ) :
    sourcePNorm 1 x=∑ i,|x i| := by
  simpa only [sourcePNorm,Real.norm_eq_abs,PiLp.toLp_apply] using
    PiLp.norm_eq_of_L1 (WithLp.toLp 1 x : PiLp 1 (fun _ : I => ℝ))

theorem actual_nonnegative_vector_has_source_one_norm_equal_to_sum (x : I → ℝ)
    (hx : ∀ i,0 ≤ x i) : sourcePNorm 1 x=∑ i,x i := by
  rw [actual_one_source_norm_is_sum_absolute_values]
  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
  intro i hi
  exact abs_of_nonneg (hx i)

theorem actual_euclidean_source_two_norm_equals_the_selected_euclidean_norm (x : I → ℝ) :
    sourcePNorm 2 x=l2Norm x := rfl

theorem actual_source_unit_ball_is_convex_for_every_p (p : ℝ≥0∞) [Fact (1 ≤ p)] :
    Convex ℝ {x : I → ℝ | sourcePNorm p x ≤ 1} := by
  intro x hx y hy a b ha hb hab
  change sourcePNorm p (a • x+b • y) ≤ 1
  have ht := (actual_every_source_p_norm_has_all_three_norm_axioms p (a • x) (b • y) 1).2.2
  have hax := (actual_every_source_p_norm_has_all_three_norm_axioms p x y a).2.1
  have hby := (actual_every_source_p_norm_has_all_three_norm_axioms p y x b).2.1
  rw [hax,hby,abs_of_nonneg ha,abs_of_nonneg hb] at ht
  calc
    sourcePNorm p (a • x+b • y) ≤ a*sourcePNorm p x+b*sourcePNorm p y := ht
    _  ≤  a*1+b*1 := add_le_add (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hx ha) (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hy hb)
    _ = 1 := by nlinarith

theorem actual_source_unit_ball_is_symmetric_for_every_p (p : ℝ≥0∞) [Fact (1 ≤ p)]
    (x : I → ℝ) : sourcePNorm p (-x)=sourcePNorm p x ∧
    ((-x)∈{y : I → ℝ | sourcePNorm p y ≤ 1} ↔ x∈{y : I → ℝ | sourcePNorm p y ≤ 1}) := by
  have h : sourcePNorm p (-x)=sourcePNorm p x := by simp [sourcePNorm]
  exact ⟨h,by simp only [mem_setOf_eq,h]⟩

theorem actual_source_unit_balls_have_the_printed_nesting :
    {x : I → ℝ | sourcePNorm 1 x ≤ 1}⊆{x | sourcePNorm 2 x ≤ 1} ∧
    {x : I → ℝ | sourcePNorm 2 x ≤ 1}⊆{x | sourcePNorm ∞ x ≤ 1} := by
  constructor
  · intro x hx
    change l2Norm x ≤ 1
    have h := CompleteFoundationsNormExercises.actual_euclidean_norm_at_most_one_norm x
    exact h.trans hx
  · intro x hx
    change sourcePNorm ∞ x ≤ 1
    rw [(actual_infinity_source_norm_is_the_coordinate_supremum x).1]
    exact (CompleteFoundationsNormExercises.actual_infinity_norm_at_most_euclidean_norm x).trans hx

theorem actual_source_p_norm_unit_ball_is_exactly_a_norm_closed_ball (p : ℝ≥0∞)
    [Fact (1 ≤ p)] (x : I → ℝ) :
    sourcePNorm p x ≤ 1 ↔
      (WithLp.toLp p x : PiLp p (fun _ : I => ℝ))∈Metric.closedBall 0 1 := by
  simp only [Metric.mem_closedBall,dist_zero_right,sourcePNorm]
end Finite

def sourceExample : Fin 2 → ℝ := ![3,-4]

theorem actual_printed_vector_has_one_norm_seven : sourcePNorm 1 sourceExample=7 := by
  rw [actual_one_source_norm_is_sum_absolute_values]
  norm_num [sourceExample,Fin.sum_univ_two]

theorem actual_printed_vector_has_two_norm_five : sourcePNorm 2 sourceExample=5 := by
  rw [actual_euclidean_source_two_norm_equals_the_selected_euclidean_norm]
  have hs := actual_l2_norm_squared sourceExample
  norm_num [sourceExample,Fin.sum_univ_two] at hs
  have hn : 0 ≤ l2Norm sourceExample := norm_nonneg _
  have hsq : l2Norm sourceExample^2=25 := hs
  nlinarith [hsq]

theorem actual_printed_vector_has_infinity_norm_four : sourcePNorm ∞ sourceExample=4 := by
  rw [(actual_infinity_source_norm_is_the_coordinate_supremum sourceExample).1]
  apply le_antisymm
  · apply (pi_norm_le_iff_of_nonneg (by norm_num : (0:ℝ) ≤ 4)).mpr
    intro i
    fin_cases i <;> norm_num [sourceExample]
  · have h := norm_le_pi_norm sourceExample 1
    norm_num [sourceExample] at h
    exact h

theorem actual_two_dimensional_one_ball_is_the_printed_diamond :
    {x : Fin 2 → ℝ | sourcePNorm 1 x ≤ 1}={x | |x 0|+|x 1| ≤ 1} := by
  ext x
  simp [actual_one_source_norm_is_sum_absolute_values,Fin.sum_univ_two]

theorem actual_two_dimensional_two_ball_is_the_printed_disc :
    {x : Fin 2 → ℝ | sourcePNorm 2 x ≤ 1}={x | (x 0)^2+(x 1)^2 ≤ 1} := by
  ext x
  change l2Norm x ≤ 1 ↔ (x 0)^2+(x 1)^2 ≤ 1
  have hs := actual_l2_norm_squared x
  simp only [Fin.sum_univ_two] at hs
  have hn : 0 ≤ l2Norm x := norm_nonneg _
  constructor <;> intro h <;> nlinarith

theorem actual_two_dimensional_infinity_ball_is_the_printed_square :
    {x : Fin 2 → ℝ | sourcePNorm ∞ x ≤ 1}={x | |x 0| ≤ 1 ∧ |x 1| ≤ 1} := by
  ext x
  change sourcePNorm ∞ x ≤ 1 ↔ |x 0| ≤ 1 ∧ |x 1| ≤ 1
  rw [(actual_infinity_source_norm_is_the_coordinate_supremum x).1]
  constructor
  · intro h
    exact ⟨(by simpa only [Real.norm_eq_abs] using (norm_le_pi_norm x 0).trans h),
      (by simpa only [Real.norm_eq_abs] using (norm_le_pi_norm x 1).trans h)⟩
  · rintro ⟨h0,h1⟩
    apply (pi_norm_le_iff_of_nonneg (by norm_num : (0:ℝ) ≤ 1)).mpr
    simpa only [Real.norm_eq_abs, Fin.forall_fin_two] using And.intro h0 h1

end SafeLearning.CompleteFoundationsLiteralNorm28

section Euclidean
variable {I : Type*} [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]

theorem actual_bounded_disturbance_has_the_literal_dual_row_bound
    (a d : I → ℝ) (dbar : ℝ) (hd : l2Norm d≤dbar) :
    |a ⬝ᵥ d|≤l2Norm a*dbar := by
  have h := abs_real_inner_le_norm (euclidean a) (euclidean d)
  rw [actual_euclidean_pairing_is_dot] at h
  exact h.trans (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hd (norm_nonneg _))

theorem actual_ball_actuator_support_has_the_literal_attained_maximum
    (b : I → ℝ) (umax : ℝ) (hu : 0≤umax) :
    IsGreatest ((fun u : I → ℝ => b ⬝ᵥ u) '' {u | l2Norm u≤umax})
      (umax*l2Norm b) := by
  have hg : IsGreatest ((fun u => ⟪euclidean b,u⟫) '' {u : EuclideanSpace ℝ I | ‖u-0‖≤umax})
      (⟪euclidean b,(0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ I)⟫+umax*‖euclidean b‖) := by
    obtain ⟨point,hp,he⟩ := CompleteFoundationsGeometry.linear_ball_attainment (euclidean b) 0 umax hu
    refine ⟨⟨point,hp,he⟩,?_⟩
    rintro _ ⟨other,ho,rfl⟩
    exact CompleteFoundationsGeometry.linear_ball_upper_bound (euclidean b) 0 other umax ho
  rcases hg.1 with ⟨u,huu,heu⟩
  refine ⟨⟨WithLp.ofLp u,?_,?_⟩,?_⟩
  · change ‖euclidean (WithLp.ofLp u)‖≤umax
    change ‖u‖≤umax
    simpa only [mem_setOf_eq,sub_zero] using huu
  · have hpair : b ⬝ᵥ WithLp.ofLp u=⟪euclidean b,u⟫ := by
      simpa only [euclidean,WithLp.toLp_ofLp] using
        (actual_euclidean_pairing_is_dot b (WithLp.ofLp u)).symm
    change b ⬝ᵥ WithLp.ofLp u=umax*l2Norm b
    rw [hpair]
    simpa only [inner_zero_right,zero_add,l2Norm] using heu
  · rintro value ⟨other,hother,rfl⟩
    have ho : euclidean other ∈ {u : EuclideanSpace ℝ I | ‖u-0‖≤umax} := by
      simpa only [mem_setOf_eq,sub_zero,l2Norm] using hother
    have hh := hg.2 ⟨euclidean other,ho,rfl⟩
    simpa only [actual_euclidean_pairing_is_dot,inner_zero_right,zero_add,l2Norm] using hh

end Euclidean

section Classification
variable {I O : Type*} [Fintype I] [Fintype O] [DecidableEq I] [DecidableEq O]

def actualClassContrast (winner other : O) : O → ℝ := Pi.single winner 1-Pi.single other 1

theorem actual_distinct_class_contrast_has_the_printed_norm
    (winner other : O) (hdistinct : winner≠other) :
    l2Norm (actualClassContrast winner other)=Real.sqrt 2 :=
  CompleteModulesClassificationNorm.actual_distinct_class_basis_difference_has_norm_sqrt_two
    winner other hdistinct

theorem actual_class_contrast_dot_product_is_the_literal_logit_difference
    (winner other : O) (logits : O → ℝ) :
    actualClassContrast winner other ⬝ᵥ logits=logits winner-logits other := by
  simp [actualClassContrast,sub_dotProduct]

theorem actual_euclidean_lipschitz_logits_have_the_printed_margin_increment_bound
    (f : EuclideanSpace ℝ I → EuclideanSpace ℝ O) (L : ℝ≥0)
    (hf : LipschitzWith L f) (winner other : O) (hdistinct : winner≠other)
    (x δ : EuclideanSpace ℝ I) :
    |((f (x+δ)) winner-(f (x+δ)) other)-((f x) winner-(f x) other)|≤
      Real.sqrt 2*(L:ℝ)*‖δ‖ := by
  let logits : EuclideanSpace ℝ I → O → ℝ := fun z => WithLp.ofLp (f z)
  have hgain : ∀ first second,
      ‖WithLp.toLp 2 (logits first-logits second)‖≤(L:ℝ)*dist first second := by
    intro first second
    have he : (WithLp.toLp 2 (logits first-logits second) : EuclideanSpace ℝ O)=f first-f second := by
      ext i
      rfl
    rw [he]
    simpa only [dist_eq_norm] using hf.dist_le_mul first second
  have h := CompleteModulesGeneralMargin.actual_arbitrary_logit_global_gain_certifies_gap_gain
    logits (L:ℝ) hgain winner other hdistinct (x+δ) x
  simpa only [logits,dist_eq_norm,add_sub_cancel_left] using h

end Classification

section InverseMetric
variable {I : Type*} [Fintype I] [DecidableEq I]

def actualInverseInner (H : Matrix I I ℝ) (u v : I → ℝ) : ℝ := u ⬝ᵥ (H⁻¹ *ᵥ v)

theorem actual_positive_metric_inverse_form_has_every_inner_product_axiom
    (H : Matrix I I ℝ) (hH : H.PosDef) (u v w : I → ℝ) (a : ℝ) :
    H⁻¹.PosDef ∧
    actualInverseInner H u v=actualInverseInner H v u ∧
    actualInverseInner H (u+v) w=actualInverseInner H u w+actualInverseInner H v w ∧
    actualInverseInner H u (v+w)=actualInverseInner H u v+actualInverseInner H u w ∧
    actualInverseInner H (a • u) v=a*actualInverseInner H u v ∧
    actualInverseInner H u (a • v)=a*actualInverseInner H u v ∧
    (u≠0 → 0<actualInverseInner H u u) := by
  have hInv := hH.inv
  have ht : (H⁻¹).transpose=H⁻¹ := by
    simpa only [Matrix.conjTranspose_eq_transpose_of_trivial] using hInv.isHermitian.eq
  refine ⟨hInv,?_,?_,?_,?_,?_,?_⟩
  · dsimp [actualInverseInner]
    rw [Matrix.dotProduct_mulVec,←Matrix.mulVec_transpose,ht,dotProduct_comm]
  · simp [actualInverseInner,add_dotProduct]
  · simp [actualInverseInner,Matrix.mulVec_add,dotProduct_add]
  · simp [actualInverseInner,smul_dotProduct]
  · simp [actualInverseInner,Matrix.mulVec_smul,dotProduct_smul]
  · intro hu
    simpa only [actualInverseInner,star_trivial] using hInv.dotProduct_mulVec_pos hu

theorem actual_cpo_source_q_s_product_bounds_the_true_cross_form_square
    (H : Matrix I I ℝ) (hH : H.PosDef) (g b : I → ℝ) :
    (g ⬝ᵥ (H⁻¹ *ᵥ g))*(b ⬝ᵥ (H⁻¹ *ᵥ b))≥(g ⬝ᵥ (H⁻¹ *ᵥ b))^2 := by
  have h := hH.inv.star_dotProduct_mulVec_mul_le g b
  simpa only [star_trivial,pow_two] using h

end InverseMetric

Definition — Norm, $\ell_p$ norms
    
      A norm satisfies (i) $\|x\|=0\iff x=0$; (ii) $\|\alpha x\|=|\alpha|\,\|x\|$; (iii) the triangle inequality $\|x+y\|\le\|x\|+\|y\|$. For $1\le p\lt\infty$, $\|x\|_p=\big(\sum_i|x_i|^p\big)^{1/p}$, and $\|x\|_\infty=\max_i|x_i|$. For $\lambda\ge0$ entrywise, $\|\lambda\|_1=\sum_i\lambda_i$. The unit ball is $\{x:\|x\|\le1\}$.

A norm satisfies (i) $\|x\|=0\iff x=0$; (ii) $\|\alpha x\|=|\alpha|\,\|x\|$; (iii) the triangle inequality $\|x+y\|\le\|x\|+\|y\|$. For $1\le p\lt\infty$, $\|x\|_p=\big(\sum_i|x_i|^p\big)^{1/p}$, and $\|x\|_\infty=\max_i|x_i|$. For $\lambda\ge0$ entrywise, $\|\lambda\|_1=\sum_i\lambda_i$. The unit ball is $\{x:\|x\|\le1\}$.

Example. $x=(3,-4)$: $\|x\|_1=7$, $\|x\|_2=5$, $\|x\|_\infty=4$. The unit balls are a diamond, a disc and a square, nested as $\{\|x\|_1\le1\}\subseteq\{\|x\|_2\le1\}\subseteq\{\|x\|_\infty\le1\}$; all are convex and symmetric.

full_literal_context.text:
Definition — Inner product and induced length
An inner product on $\mathbb R^n$ is a function $\langle x,y\rangle\in\mathbb R$ that is (i) symmetric, (ii) linear in each argument, (iii) positive: $\langle x,x\rangle\gt0$ for $x\ne0$. It induces the length $\|x\|=\sqrt{\langle x,x\rangle}$. The standard one is $x^\top y=\sum_ix_iy_i$; a weighted one is $\langle x,y\rangle_M=x^\top My$ with $M$ symmetric positive definite (Section 4; e.g. $M=\mathrm{diag}(m_i)$, all $m_i\gt0$), with length $\|x\|_M=\sqrt{x^\top Mx}$.

Intuition and example. In the plane $x^\top y=\|x\|\,\|y\|\cos\theta$: the inner product measures alignment. For $x=(1,2)$, $y=(3,-1)$: $x^\top y=1$, $\|x\|=\sqrt5$, $\|y\|=\sqrt{10}$, $\theta\approx81.9^\circ$. With $M=\mathrm{diag}(1,4)$ (coordinate 2 counts double): $\langle x,y\rangle_M=3-8=-5$, $\|x\|_M=\sqrt{17}$, $\|y\|_M=\sqrt{13}$, an obtuse angle. Which vectors are long or perpendicular depends on the inner product.

Theorem — Cauchy–Schwarz inequality
For every inner product and all $x,y$: $\ |\langle x,y\rangle|\le\|x\|\,\|y\|$, with equality iff $x$ and $y$ are parallel.

Proof. If $y=0$ both sides are $0$. Otherwise, for every real $t$, $0\le\|x-ty\|^2=\|x\|^2-2t\langle x,y\rangle+t^2\|y\|^2$. This parabola in $t$ is smallest at $t^\star=\langle x,y\rangle/\|y\|^2$, where it equals $\|x\|^2-\langle x,y\rangle^2/\|y\|^2\ge0$. Equality forces $x=t^\star y$. $\square$ Only (i)–(iii) were used, so it holds for weighted inner products and for functions (Section 8).

Fact — Maximising a linear function over a ball
$\max_{\|u\|\le1}c^\top u=\|c\|$, attained at $u=c/\|c\|$ if $c\ne0$ (for $c=0$ every $u$ is a maximiser); over $\|u-u_0\|\le r$, $r\ge0$, the maximum is $c^\top u_0+r\|c\|$.

Uses. $|a^\top d|\le\|a\|\bar d$ for a disturbance with $\|d\|\le\bar d$, and $\max_{\|u\|\le u_{\max}}b^\top u=u_{\max}\|b\|$. A logit difference is $(e_y-e_j)^\top f$ with $\|e_y-e_j\|=\sqrt2$, so an $L$-Lipschitz $f$ moves the margin by at most $\sqrt2L\|\delta\|$ (the $\sqrt2$ of Module 12's certified radius). For $H\succ0$, $u^\top H^{-1}v$ is an inner product, and for CPO's $q=g^\top H^{-1}g$, $r=g^\top H^{-1}b$, $s=b^\top H^{-1}b$ Cauchy–Schwarz reads $qs\ge r^2$.

Fact — AM–GM and Young's inequality
For $a,b\ge0$: $\sqrt{ab}\le\tfrac12(a+b)$, equality iff $a=b$ (expand $(\sqrt a-\sqrt b)^2\ge0$). Hence $u+c/u\ge2\sqrt c$ for $u,c\gt0$, with equality at $u=\sqrt c$, and $2|ab|\le\varepsilon a^2+b^2/\varepsilon$ for every $\varepsilon\gt0$ (splitting a cross term into squares).

1.2 Norms and their unit balls

Definition — Norm, $\ell_p$ norms
A norm satisfies (i) $\|x\|=0\iff x=0$; (ii) $\|\alpha x\|=|\alpha|\,\|x\|$; (iii) the triangle inequality $\|x+y\|\le\|x\|+\|y\|$. For $1\le p\lt\infty$, $\|x\|_p=\big(\sum_i|x_i|^p\big)^{1/p}$, and $\|x\|_\infty=\max_i|x_i|$. For $\lambda\ge0$ entrywise, $\|\lambda\|_1=\sum_i\lambda_i$. The unit ball is $\{x:\|x\|\le1\}$.

Example. $x=(3,-4)$: $\|x\|_1=7$, $\|x\|_2=5$, $\|x\|_\infty=4$. The unit balls are a diamond, a disc and a square, nested as $\{\|x\|_1\le1\}\subseteq\{\|x\|_2\le1\}\subseteq\{\|x\|_\infty\le1\}$; all are convex and symmetric.

Triangle inequality for $\ell_2$ from Cauchy–Schwarz: $\|x+y\|^2=\|x\|^2+2x^\top y+\|y\|^2\le(\|x\|+\|y\|)^2$. The reverse triangle inequality $\big|\,\|x\|-\|y\|\,\big|\le\|x-y\|$ follows from $\|x\|\le\|x-y\|+\|y\|$ and symmetry: every norm is 1-Lipschitz. Stacked vectors $z=(x,u)$: $\|z\|_2^2=\|x\|_2^2+\|u\|_2^2$, $\|z\|_1=\|x\|_1+\|u\|_1$, $\|z\|_\infty=\max\{\|x\|_\infty,\|u\|_\infty\}$. A punctured ball $\{u:0\lt\|u\|_2\le1\}$ excludes the centre, where $u/\|u\|_2$ is undefined.

Pitfall
For $p\lt1$ the formula is not a norm: $p=\tfrac12$ gives $\|(1,1)\|=4\gt\|(1,0)\|+\|(0,1)\|=2$. And modules switch norms (Module 11 states its Lipschitz constants in the 1-norm): always check which norm a constant refers to.
